question: Prediction of conversion from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI patients, compared at a 36-month horizon, through the MRI channel. P-211 (EBM, ADNI 1/2/3/GO) uses FreeSurfer regional volumes and thickness with demographics, baseline EMCI/LMCI and APOE4, with cognitive scores added in Comb (a) and left out in Comb (c). P-93's compared experiment is its secondary MCI-conversion task (Section 4.3): whole-brain T1 images with GAN-synthesised FDG-PET, and no cognitive or demographic input. P-93's headline task (SCD to MCI) is not the one compared. The recorded horizons differ (P-211 five years, P-93 36 months), which the rule allows.

figures.P-211: Five-year Comb (a): AUC 0.92, taken over 225 participants (85 dementia/140 MCI). No interval is printed. Hanley-McNeil over the CV sample: Q1 = 0.8519, Q2 = 0.8817, SE 0.0214, CI [0.878, 0.962]. Over a 10% test set (about 9/14): CI [0.788, 1.000]. Three-year Comb (a) on the test data: AUC 0.81 with interaction effects and 0.78 without. The 3-year cohort is 188 dementia/392 MCI. Hanley-McNeil at the test-set n (about 19/39): Q1 = 0.6807, Q2 = 0.7250, SE 0.0659, CI [0.681, 0.939]. Over the whole 3-year cohort: SE 0.0207, CI [0.769, 0.851]. Three-year 5-fold CV means, read off Figure 2(d) (the axis runs 0 to 1 over 632 px): Comb (a) about 0.75 and Comb (c) about 0.70 (point at 444/632 px). The SD error bars are about 0.01. Hanley-McNeil for 0.70 over the CV portion of the 3-year set (about 169/353): Q1 = 0.5385, Q2 = 0.5765, SE 0.0255, CI [0.650, 0.750]. Over 188/392 the CI is [0.653, 0.747]. For Comb (a) 0.75 over 169/353 the CI is [0.703, 0.797].
figures.P-93: MCI-conversion AUC 0.838 (ACC 0.780) on an independent ADNI test set, MRI only at test time. The text gives 177 subjects (96 pMCI/81 sMCI); Table 5 gives 66/93. No interval is printed. Hanley-McNeil with 96/81: Q1 = 0.7212, Q2 = 0.7641, SE 0.0298, CI [0.780, 0.896]. With 93/66: SE 0.0310, CI [0.777, 0.899].

matched_figure_check: There are two matched figures, and they point in opposite directions. (1) The horizon-matched figure printed in the text is P-211's 3-year test AUC, 0.81 (0.78 without interactions). 0.81 lies inside P-93's [0.780, 0.896], and 0.838 lies inside P-211's 3-year intervals ([0.681, 0.939] at the test n; [0.769, 0.851] over the whole cohort). These agree, which dissolves the recorded gap: 0.92 is P-211's five-year figure. (2) The figure matched on both horizon and channel is P-211's Comb (c), which uses MRI plus demographics/APOE4 and no cognitive scores. Its 3-year value is only plotted (Figure 2d), at about 0.70. That lies outside P-93's interval, and P-93's 0.838 lies outside Comb (c)'s CV interval [0.650, 0.750]: z = 0.138/sqrt(0.0298^2 + 0.0255^2) = 3.52. So on the best-matched cell there is a gap in the reverse direction, with P-93 higher. P-211's own plotted 3-year Comb (a) CV mean (about 0.75) also falls below P-93's interval, while its text-reported test figures for Comb (a) (0.78/0.81) agree with P-93. The same Figure 2(d) reading bears on C-149 and C-150, whose readers used only the 0.81.
performance_validity: Passes: no compared figure reaches 0.97 (P-211's highest is 0.92, P-93's is 0.838).

candidate_explanations.difference: Input representation for the reverse gap on the matched cell: P-93 scores whole-brain T1 images with GAN-synthesised PET features in a deep model, while P-211's Comb (c) scores tabular FreeSurfer regional measures with demographics and APOE4 in an EBM.
candidate_explanations.quote: Comb. (c) MRI-driven biomarkers, plus age, gender, education, diagnose at baseline, and APOE4.

candidate_explanations.difference: Training design: P-93 trains on 939 ADNI subjects with complete MRI and PET, including cognitively normal and AD participants pooled into the two classes, and tests on independent MRI-only MCI subjects. P-211 trains on MCI patients only, with SMOTE, a 90/10 split and 5-fold CV.
candidate_explanations.quote: That is, sMCI and sCN are treated as the negative category, pMCI and AD are used as the positive category.

candidate_explanations.difference: Label construction at 3 years: P-211 attributes its 3-year low point to patients who convert after three years being counted as false positives, whereas P-93 keeps only MCI subjects whose 36-month status is clear.
candidate_explanations.quote: these false positives represent individuals whose diagnostic classification did not change during the short-term follow-up period, despite the disease progressing and eventually reaching the dementia stage at a later time point

candidate_explanations.difference: Case mix and test-set size: P-93's test set is near-balanced (96 pMCI/81 sMCI in the text, 93/66 in Table 5, an internal inconsistency). P-211's 3-year set is 188 dementia/392 MCI.
candidate_explanations.quote: And 177 subjects (including 81 sMCI and 96 pMCI) with only MRI are used as independent test data.

candidate_explanations.difference: Evaluation split within P-211: its 3-year test-set figures for Comb (a) (0.78/0.81) are higher than its plotted CV mean (about 0.75), so P-211's 3-year estimate depends on the split. The Comb (c) value is only plotted.
candidate_explanations.quote: were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects)

reason: The recorded gap (0.92 vs 0.838) sets P-211's five-year AUC against a 36-month result. At the matched horizon, P-211's printed 3-year AUC (0.81) agrees with P-93 in both directions, so the recorded disagreement dissolves. On the cell matched for both horizon and channel, P-211's MRI-without-cognition model (Comb c) is plotted at about 0.70. That is below P-93's 0.838 beyond uncertainty (z = 3.5), so a reverse-direction gap remains. It rests on a value read off a figure, not printed as a number, and none of the candidate explanations is shown to be sufficient, so the pair is borderline.

quotes.quote: The five-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of first at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.
A similar trend was observed in the lines of the Comb (c), although with different magnitudes, and the line of Comb (a) being slightly smaller than that of Comb (c).

The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects), respectively.
All EBMs were tested with the 5-fold cross validation.
subjects with pMCI would convert to AD within 36 months after baseline and subjects with sMCI remain stable.
Figure 4 suggests that our JSRL achieves the best AUC of 0.838 and ACC of 0.780
we used only neuroimaging data for prediction, without considering the demographic information (e.g., age, gender, and education)
